# System Composer Modal Composition Implementation Roadmap

- Status: `completed`
- Updated: `2026-07-25T15:05:07Z`

## Objective

Replace drag-based System Composer authoring with accessible container-scoped asset selection, preserve complete click-based placement and ordering capabilities, and lazily load only the property detail required by the active editor surface.

## Discovery

The shared Composer currently registers drag, drop, and sort behavior throughout the Canvas and eagerly expands every catalog item with its configuration schema and defaults. Canonical containment already lives in ordered AssetPlacement records, so the interaction can become modal and command driven without changing persisted hierarchy. The shared ModalDialog already owns accessible focus containment and restoration.

### Constraints

- Preserve canonical AssetPlacement and named-slot semantics; do not create a renderer-owned hierarchy.
- Keep desktop and thin-client behavior in the shared UI and carry new reads through API and Electron IPC/preload parity.
- Retain saved instance configuration values in the active revision because preview, validation, undo, and saving require the complete draft.
- Keep executable code and backing-resource bytes outside Asset Kernel metadata and preserve existing preview security boundaries.
- Use the shared ModalDialog and provide complete keyboard and focus behavior.
- Run focused tests for internal chunks and repository-wide completion gates only once after the increment is complete.

## High-level decisions

### Composer modal composition and lazy-loading boundary

How completely should the drag replacement and selected-property lazy loading be implemented?

A UI-only replacement would remove drag registrations but retain the eager property payload, while fully partial revisions would unnecessarily disrupt preview, undo, and immutable revision semantics.

- Status: `approved`
- Selected option: `complete-click-composition-selected-detail`

| Option | Summary | Recommended | Tradeoffs | Consequences |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Complete click-based Composer with true lazy properties (complete-click-composition-selected-detail) | Use container-scoped asset modals, explicit click-based move and order actions, on-demand layouts and compatible candidates, lightweight structural summaries, and exact selected-definition detail reads. | yes | Touches contracts, application reads, both transports, shared UI, tests, and documentation in one cohesive vertical change.; Preserves complete saved draft configuration while removing property schemas and defaults from the eager catalog payload. | All drag code and dnd-kit dependencies can be removed.; Adding, moving, and ordering assets remain accessible without pointer dragging.; Only the selected asset property detail and active root Styling detail remain loaded. |
| UI-only modal conversion (ui-only-modal) | Replace the palette and drag controls but retain the existing full Composer catalog payload. | no | Smaller transport change.; Does not satisfy true property lazy loading or the requested memory reduction. | Every catalog asset still loads its property schema and defaults before selection. |
| Fully partial revision loading (fully-partial-revisions) | Fetch hierarchy, saved configuration, and definition data independently for each selected instance. | no | Lowest theoretical retained payload.; Requires a broad persistence, concurrency, undo, preview, and draft-merge redesign. | Accurate complete previews and immutable revision editing become materially more complex. |

## Increment 1: Complete modal-based, lazily loaded System Composer

- Id: `complete-modal-composer`
- Status: `completed`
- Dependencies: None

Deliver the complete shared click-based composition experience and its selected-detail loading boundary without changing canonical placement, preview, revision, or security semantics.

### Work packages

- **Composer summary and exact-detail boundary** (`summary-detail-contracts`): Lightweight structural summaries support Canvas, Layers, compatibility, and Connections while an exact workspace-scoped operation loads property schemas and defaults only for the selected editor surface.
- **Container-scoped modal composition** (`modal-composition`): Every exact container exposes Add element, the shared modal selects a destination region and compatible new or unassigned asset, and successful insertion selects, focuses, and reveals the child.
- **Complete non-drag placement controls** (`non-drag-complete-controls`): Layouts move to a collapsible on-demand bar, placed assets retain explicit move and ordering controls, nonvisual resources remain discoverable, and all drag code and dependencies are removed.
- **Lazy-loading, performance, and host parity** (`performance-and-host-parity`): Desktop and thin client share stale-safe selected-detail loading, bounded modal paging, on-demand layouts and Styling detail, stable hierarchy rendering, and verified request/payload behavior.

### Deliverables

- Lightweight Composer summary and exact-definition detail contracts and use cases
- HTTP and Electron IPC/preload/client parity for exact detail reads
- Shared accessible asset-selection modal scoped to an exact parent and named region
- Click-based add, reuse, move, and deterministic ordering behavior
- Collapsible on-demand layout bar below Design and Connections
- Selected-only property and active-only Styling detail loading with stale-response protection
- Removal of Asset Palette drag interactions, drag adapters, drag tests, and dnd-kit dependencies
- Focused contract, application, transport, shared UI, hierarchy, preview, accessibility, request-count, and regression tests
- Updated ADR, architecture, context, README, and contributor guidance

| `shared-host-parity`: Desktop and thin client expose identical summary, detail, modal composition, loading, empty, error, keyboard, focus-restoration, and failure behavior through their real IPC and HTTP client boundaries. | local | passed (test) |

### Verification

- Run focused Composer contract and application tests for lightweight summaries, exact detail, workspace isolation, exact Foundation fallback, compatibility, bounds, and sanitized failures.
- Run focused API, IPC, preload, desktop-client, thin-client-client, and transport-parity tests for summary and exact-detail reads.
- Run focused shared UI tests for modal accessibility, region choice, paged search, add/reuse/focus, move/order, layout disclosure, nonvisual resource discovery, and removal of drag behavior.
- Run focused request-count, stale-response, retained-detail, nested hierarchy, recursive preview, and representative reference-system regression tests.
- After all internal work packages pass, run the applicable desktop/thin-client builds and npm run docs:check, npm run architecture:check, npm run agent-support:check, npm run package, and npm test once as increment completion gates.

### Rollback

Restore the previous shared Composer surface and eager catalog client while preserving all existing immutable revisions, placements, definitions, configurations, and layout selections. The additive exact-detail read can remain unused safely; rollback must not flatten or rewrite canonical hierarchy.

### Excluded

- Changing canonical AssetPlacement, AssetBinding, immutable revision, build, release, or runtime semantics
- Freeform Canvas positioning, user-authored slots, arbitrary dimensions, or unbounded CSS/code editing
- Partial persistence of revision instance values or a new renderer-owned hierarchy
- Execution of untrusted backing resources, deployment changes, collaboration, marketplace, or unrelated Asset Library redesign
- Virtualizing away selected or expanded hierarchy nodes in a way that hides canonical composition
